clock_rules: retrieved_at records our acquisition time and never substitutes for published_at or effective_at.
Every normalized record preserves effective_at, published_at, first_observed_at and retrieved_at when available.
Corrections produce a new version; they do not overwrite the prior observed value.
Deletion creates a tombstone only after a successful complete snapshot or source-specific deletion event.
Source failure, empty response and zero records are separate states.
pagination_rules: Use stable order by immutable object ID where supported.
Record every page URL/parameters, page hash, count and exceeded-limit flag.
Run a second count/reconciliation query after paginated retrieval.
Reject snapshots with duplicate object IDs, page gaps or unstable count beyond the registered tolerance.
schema_rules: Fingerprint ordered field names, types, aliases, nullability and coded domains.
Block normalization when critical fields disappear or change type.
Allow additive noncritical fields only after schema-drift evidence is recorded.
Preserve source field names in raw and map them to versioned canonical primitives.
privacy_rules: Exclude personal names and contact fields not necessary for entity/location research.
Published contact information is not outreach consent.
Hash or quarantine sensitive raw fields where retention is not justified.
minimum_replay_test: raw bytes plus collector version must deterministically reproduce normalized primitives and manifest hashes
